question.text: An acidified solution of potassium chromate was layered with an equal volume of amyl alcohol. When it was shaken after the addition of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo></math> a blue alcohol layer was obtained. The blue color is due to the formation of a chromium (VI) compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>'</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mo>'</mo></math>. What is the number of oxygen atoms bonded to chromium through only single bonds in a molecule of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math>?

solution.text:
K2CrO4→H+/H2O2CrO5(Deep Blue solution)

No. of oxygen atom bonded with chromium with single bond is (4).
